title: Getting Started
text: Getting Started Install the correct app variant, open the four-tab dashboard and begin with the actual file browser. 1. Download the current package Use the verified rolling release . Choose APP_LAUNCHSTATION.zip for standard PS2 controls or APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS.zip for the inherited PS3/PS4 controller variant. Matching .psu packages support memory-card installation via PSU Paste. Device-specific hardware testing is separate from successful compilation. 2. Install the app folder mc0:/ └── APP_LAUNCHSTATION/ ├── LAUNCHSTATION.ELF ├── title.cfg ├── BGM.ADP └── WLE-UPDATE-CA.PEM Extract the ZIP as a folder or install the matching PSU. Preserve existing settings and customized sidecars if upgrading. The DS package has its own folder and LAUNCHSTATION-DS.ELF . BGM is optional to run; the current packages include it. 3. Use the four main tabs Use L1/R1 to move between Home, Files, Tools and Settings . Home includes the Applications library and, once known, Last folder. Files opens the native browser immediately ; choose a drive or folder there. Tools contains classic MISC commands and specialist utilities. Current UI map . 4. Open a device Start in Files, at the device root. Memory cards, USB/MASS, MMCE, MX4SIO, internal HDD/ATA, iLink and configured network devices have distinct availability rules. Not checked usually means opening the device must start a lazy-loaded driver. USB units can change numbering. Avoid simultaneous writes across recovery or backup operations. 5. Find applications Use Home > Applications for the library, or browse and launch an ELF directly from Files. Under Settings > Home & applications > Application library , configure application folders and refresh the library. The default roots currently include mc:/APPS , mc:/BOOT , mass:/APPS and mass:/BOOT , one level deep. Applications outside these folders can still launch from Files. 6. Optional external cores Neutrino is needed for PS2 .ISO ; POPStarter for PS1 .VCD ; Ember for PS1 .CUE / .BIN / .EXE in its save-safe game-folder layout. These external programs and game/BIOS data are not bundled. Read the specific guide before your first handoff. 7. Configure MMCE backups if needed Choose a local backup destination under Settings > Storage & devices > MMCE backups . Link Google Drive only if desired. A verified snapshot can be recovered to a new file, not directly over an active MMCE card. See MMCE recovery . 8. Save and update safely Settings has explicit Save/Discard semantics. Before upgrading, retain a backup of your configuration and current working ELF. The native updater verifies the rolling package and stages changes, with an original executable recovery copy for rollback.

title: Install & Update
text: Install & Update Install the matching app package and preserve your existing configuration and customized files. Standard rolling package mc0:/ └── APP_LAUNCHSTATION/ ├── LAUNCHSTATION.ELF ├── title.cfg ├── BGM.ADP └── WLE-UPDATE-CA.PEM Both standard ZIP and PSU packages contain those four files. DS34 controller packages use APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS with LAUNCHSTATION-DS.ELF. The ELF alone can run the dashboard, but the packaged updater CA supports native verified HTTPS updating; BGM.ADP is optional for a standalone installation. Choose your installer Download the matching ZIP/PSU from Downloads & Releases . Extract the ZIP app folder to readable storage or use the File Browser PSU Paste command to install a PSU on a memory card. Keep a separate copy of your previous working ELF, settings and customized sidecars. Configuration LAUNCHSTATION retains classic LAUNCHELF.CNF support and its dashboard settings store. The saved path can be configured next to the ELF, in a selected folder or on a memory-card SYS-CONF location. See Configuration . Google Drive remains opt-in Linking needs no setup files: choose Link Google Drive and enter the shown code at google.com/device. Launchstation then stores a refresh token in WLE-CLOUD.TOK. Do not publish your token or include it in a bug report. Google Drive is optional for ordinary files and local MMCE history. Native updates and rollback The current in-app updater checks release ancestry, downloads the matching standard or DS34 PSU, validates the published SHA-256 and ELF, stages replacement and keeps a .BAK copy of the preceding executable. It restores missing only CA/BGM sidecars from the verified four-file PSU without overwriting customized ones. Existing interrupted .UPDATE or .PACKAGE artifacts require manual resolution. Restart LAUNCHSTATION to use installed code; older clients may need a one-time manual package update. Preserve a hardware-tested baseline If a newer rolling build regresses on your console, retain the 2026-10-08 USB-tested baseline and collect hardware details before retrying. Compiled CI success is distinct from successful console validation.

title: Downloads & Releases
text: Downloads & Releases Four installable app packages, built from the same commit. Latest automated build GitHub Actions Release assets Package Packed executable Installation APP_LAUNCHSTATION.zip LAUNCHSTATION.ELF Extract APP_LAUNCHSTATION/ to a supported filesystem. APP_LAUNCHSTATION.psu LAUNCHSTATION.ELF Use PSU Paste to install APP_LAUNCHSTATION/ on a memory card. APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS.zip LAUNCHSTATION-DS.ELF Extract APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS/ to a supported filesystem. APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS.psu LAUNCHSTATION-DS.ELF Use PSU Paste to install APP_LAUNCHSTATION-DS/ on a memory card. Each app folder contains its packed executable, title.cfg , WLE-UPDATE-CA.PEM for verified HTTPS updates, and BGM.ADP for background music. ZIP and PSU payloads match. Back up any existing settings before replacing an app folder. DualShock build The -DS packages enable the inherited PS3/PS4 USB/Bluetooth controller drivers. The standard packages use the standard PS2 pad driver. Build checks do not establish controller and storage coexistence on a real console. Integrity and native updates The native updater first verifies that the published release descends from the running Git commit (and refuses older, divergent or unverifiable updates). It then selects the PSU matching its controller variant, verifies GitHub's SHA-256 asset digest, extracts only the matching ELF, and validates its PS2 ELF header before staged replacement with rollback. Older updater builds expecting standalone ELFs or two-file PSUs require one manual installation of the new package before the four-file PSU can be used by the native updater. Subsequent native updates restore missing updater CA/BGM sidecars from the verified four-file PSU and replace the ELF; existing/custom sidecars are never overwritten. Updates from legacy two-file PSUs remain ELF-only. For bug reports, record the commit and package or ELF SHA-256. The app packages include music and the update CA; standalone ELF installations can copy res/music.sad as BGM.ADP and res/WLE-UPDATE-CA.PEM alongside the ELF. Google Drive account configuration and its separate CA setup remain optional and are not bundled. Offline documentation can be generated with python docs-site/build.py --out build/docs --zip build/Launchstation-Documentation.zip . Rolling publication policy The rolling latest tag is refreshed by successful verified master CI publication, including docs-only commits. The four ZIP/PSU variants come from the same source commit and have recorded checksums. If a new build behaves differently on a particular PS2, use the known-good preserved baseline release and report console model, source hash, device and reproduction steps. CI and package integrity do not substitute for real hardware acceptance. See preserved USB-tested baseline .

Four top-level tabs Tab Behavior in current builds Home Continue carousel, pinned/recent/favorite applications, Applications library shortcut, Last folder shortcut when available, and optional configured launch-key shortcuts. Files Opens the native File Browser directly inside the dashboard frame. Browse drives and folders, operate on files and return to the same folder/selection after switching tabs. title: File Browser
text: File Browser Files is a first-class, persistent dashboard tab using the native browser. The separate modal browser is also available from Tools; classic wLaunchELF file operations remain supported through the shared backends. Tab and folder continuity Files opens directly into the browser without a separate landing page. L1/R1 switches top-level dashboard tabs; returning preserves the browser folder and selection. The Home tab provides the Last folder shortcut. MISC commands are grouped under Tools, not listed as independent top-level tabs. Opening files .PNG , .JPG , .JPEG — open in the native dashboard image viewer. PNG uses the existing bounded libpng decoder; JPEG uses a bounded libjpeg path derived from the historical wLaunchELF JPG support. Image viewer controls: Left/Right browse other PNG/JPG/JPEG images in the current sorted folder (wrapping at either end), Up/Down rotate 90 degrees, L2/R2 zoom, left stick pans while zoomed, Square toggles fullscreen, Start toggles slideshow, L1/R1 changes the 1-60 second slideshow delay, Select resets the view, and Confirm/Back closes the viewer. Slideshow uses the same mixed-format folder order. .ELF , .XLF , .KELF — executable launch path. .VCD — POPStarter PS1 handoff. .CUE , .BIN , PS1 .EXE — Ember when the image is directly inside <umbrella>/games/<Game>/ . The umbrella name is not fixed. .ISO — Neutrino PS2 handoff. Text/config formats — dashboard Text Editor. Folders — enter folder. Ember handoff USB Ember launches use a clean IOP handoff. Launchstation finishes background I/O and audio, resets the IOP, and rebuilds only the USB filesystem stack before starting Ember. The launcher deliberately does not reload its homebrew SIO2MAN/PADMAN modules; Ember loads the ROM pad modules itself. This avoids the hardware-observed pad init rc=-1 conflict while keeping the selected USB game tree mounted again before Ember starts. Operations Triangle opens contextual operations. Depending on device and file type, the browser can copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, create folders, calculate size, edit or organize timestamps, work with PSU saves, mount VMC images, edit text or invoke specialist tools. Selection Square marks entries. Operations apply to the marked set; otherwise they apply to the focused entry. Classic exploit-protection checks remain for sensitive memory-card paths. Sorting The dashboard browser supports As Stored, Name, Game Title, Size, Date-Time and Kind . Sorted modes can be Ascending or Descending. Folders remain grouped first even in descending order. Classic file-browser improvements (October 2026) The classic modal File Browser's L1 display/sort menu now supports reversible sorting: choose Filename (D-pad Down), Game title (Left) or Timestamp (Up); press the same direction again to reverse its order. Right selects No sort . Triangle returns to the browser. Folders remain ahead of files and ELF entries ahead of other files in both directions. The dashboard Files tab already has its own independent six-mode ascending/descending sort selector. In memory-card save titles, Launchstation now respects icon.sys 's title line-break offset for PS2 save folders and PSU archives, adding a separator without splitting Shift-JIS characters or duplicating existing spaces. The *Tuna Date operation for a selected real MC folder is now inside Folder dates... , with Manual, A-Z, Z-A and SAS ordering. It is deliberately absent when the selection is not an eligible physical memory-card folder; the older HDD/PFS date functions are unchanged. Size and date-time Size and date-time occupy independent columns with an explicit gutter. Seconds are retained. Filename width is calculated from actual metadata width so full timestamps fit rather than being shortened. Root devices Root entries represent supported device classes. Demand-loaded cards can be opened while in Not checked state; the opening action triggers the stack and refreshes device state. USB discovery does not assume a permanent mass0: .

title: Applications
text: Applications Library Applications is the full library nested under Home, not an extra top-level tab. Use Home > Applications to browse configured folders, favorites, pinned apps and recents. Home integration The Continue carousel surfaces pinned, recent and favorite applications; Last folder is available after a valid path has been visited. SELECT cycles Grid, List and Carousel in the Applications library. Filters include All, Favorites and device categories. What is scanned Only configured Application folders are scanned. Defaults: mc:/APPS/ mc:/BOOT/ mass:/APPS/ mass:/BOOT/ Each configured root includes one subfolder level. This avoids silently crawling every attached filesystem. Manage scan roots Open Settings → Home & applications → Application library → Application folders... . Each current root is labeled “this folder + one subfolder.” Add Folder chooses an exact root; Restore Defaults restores the standard memory-card and mass roots. Presentation The dashboard can show application metadata and artwork when present. Long titles use bounded marquee behavior. Unfocused app rendering has stable alpha/scissor state so memory-card-style icons do not become half rendered. Artwork & covers Every application gets a default tile : a generated icon tinted per app. Its style is set in Settings > Customize theme > Icons > Default app icon . To show your own cover instead, add a PNG in one of the places below. Settings > Home & applications > Application artwork must be On. Image format PNG only (transparency is supported). title: Launch Arguments
text: Launch Arguments Launchstation can cache a user argument list, consume a sidecar .arg file, or launch directly from a Text Editor buffer. File Browser workflow Select a Text Editor-supported argument file. Open its operations menu and choose Launch ELF with Args . Launchstation parses and caches the argument lines in memory. Select the target ELF. The cached arguments are appended after the normal handoff path. Text Editor workflow The Text Editor offers the same action for the current in-memory buffer. Unsaved edits are used, which makes it convenient for testing launch flags without repeatedly writing the argument file. Automatic sidecar arguments For an ordinary ELF launch, Launchstation checks for a same-directory sidecar whose base name matches the ELF, for example: APPS/ ├── BOOT.ELF └── BOOT.arg If arguments were already cached manually through the browser/editor action, the sidecar is ignored for that launch. Format and limits Rule Current limit One non-empty line One user argument User arguments 12 lines Characters per argument 255 Total cached argument text 2,048 bytes including terminators Line endings are stripped. Other characters on each line are preserved. argv[0] The target executable still receives the normal selected/handoff path as argv[0] ; cached user lines follow it. External-core paths such as Neutrino build their own controlled argument set and do not consume a stray normal-ELF argument cache.

title: Device Support
text: Device Support The dashboard distinguishes Ready , Not checked , Absent and Busy states instead of collapsing them into one disconnected label. Storage matrix Device Browse Demand-load PS2 ISO via Neutrino Memory card Yes No Useful as Neutrino loader location; not normal ISO storage USB / MASS Yes Yes Yes MX4SIO Yes Yes Yes MMCE Yes Yes Yes iLink / FireWire Yes Yes Yes Internal HDD (APA/PFS) Yes Yes File/app workflows; raw game layouts are backend-specific ATA/exFAT Yes Yes Yes UDPFS Where configured Network stack Yes Why Not checked is selectable A demand-loaded driver cannot know whether hardware is absent until it runs. A Not checked device therefore remains navigable; opening it triggers the existing lazy loader. A confirmed Absent card can be displayed but is skipped by focus navigation. USB units USB is labeled USB / MASS . The implementation discovers available units and does not treat mass0: as a permanent identity. USB enumeration and intermittent stalls When the USB stack starts, Launchstation probes at most four times with spaced checks, including late second-drive discovery. Each probe uses a synchronous PS2 IOP filesystem RPC: the number of retries is bounded, but a single blocked driver call cannot be timed out safely by the EE. The controller's analog light going out can indicate a stalled PAD/SIO2 or IOP session; it does not, by itself, prove a software reset. An overloaded USB power rail is also possible with two bus-powered drives. Compare behavior with one drive, a powered hub, and the older launcher baseline. Do not hot-unplug a drive during active writes. Hide unavailable devices When unavailable-device display is disabled, those cards are removed from both drawing and navigation indices; the focus rectangle does not pass through hidden/disabled cards. Tools: USB unit diagnostics Use Tools > USB unit diagnostics to inspect the last cached logical-unit mask without new I/O or explicitly probe USB unit 0 or 1 one at a time. A manual probe is a synchronous IOP filesystem call; a failed driver can block despite bounded retry logic. Logical usb0: / usb1: numbers are not physical port identifiers. Consult the USB stability audit for technical history.

Partition operations The HDD Manager can inspect APA partitions and exposes creation/removal/rename/expand/format and related maintenance operations where supported. These actions are destructive; confirm the target disk and partition before writing. Browse partitions and game information The partition list displays original APA identifiers, as in classic wLaunchELF, without querying HDL game titles on every cursor movement. Scroll or page using the D-pad and L2/R2. For a selected HDL game partition, press R1 — Game info to load its title and disc information explicitly. Injection modes Mode Behavior This partition only Inject only the selected partition from its matching header folder. Matching partitions Scan __Headers and inject folders whose partitions already exist. Matching and create missing Inject existing matches, then prompt before creating each missing valid partition. title: Network & PC
text: Network & PC Integration Network features are demand-loaded where practical so normal file-manager startup does not pay for an unused network stack. FTP The R3Z work includes an FTP workflow compatible with its modernized network stack. Start network services intentionally from Tools/settings rather than keeping them resident for every boot. MrRexD-compatible remote commands The project follows the existing R3Z PC-side command ecosystem instead of inventing an unnecessary second desktop protocol. Supported remote commands can request launch/transfer actions using the compatible client. PC game receiver / UDPFS PC game receiver and UDPFS functionality provide network-backed workflows. UDPFS is also an accepted Neutrino ISO backend when the filesystem/server and IP configuration are valid. IP configuration Network settings use the classic IP, netmask and gateway configuration model. The dashboard tracks unsaved network state separately and can write an updated IPCONFIG-style snapshot. Failure isolation Confirm physical link and adapter initialization. Confirm IP/netmask/gateway. Confirm service/filesystem discovery. Only then debug FTP, UDPFS, cloud or another upper-layer feature. Native cloud sockets have bounded connect/handshake/read/write waits. DNS resolution in PS2IP remains synchronous and is a separate hardware edge case.

title: Saves, PSU & Timestamps
text: Saves, PSU & Timestamp Tools Launchstation keeps the classic memory-card/save toolbox while making destructive actions and timestamp manipulation more explicit. PSU create and extract The browser uses explicit Create PSU and Extract PSU wording so the direction of the conversion is clear. PSU containers are useful for moving save folders while preserving PS2 metadata that ordinary host filesystems do not represent well. Copying saves Copy/paste and PSU workflows retain the specialized handling required by memory-card folders. Avoid treating a PS2 save as an arbitrary PC directory when preserving icon metadata, attributes and timestamps matters. Virtual memory cards VMC image files can be mounted through the File Browser where supported, exposing their contents through the normal file-management path. Timestamp manipulation Launchstation can edit and organize directory timestamps. This is especially useful for OSDSYS/HOSDSYS ordering and icon-based exploit folders whose position is influenced by timestamps. Organizer roots The organizer supports memory-card roots and hdd0:/__common/ . Sorting modes include manual ordering, A–Z and SAS-style timestamps; game-save handling is kept distinct where appropriate. Exploit-folder protection Dangerous modifications/deletions of known exploit-style memory-card folders trigger warnings. That guard exists because a routine rename/delete can turn a bootable exploit card into an unbootable one.

title: PS1 Images · Ember
text: PS1 Image Launching · Ember Ember is the second PS1 core beside POPStarter. The two do not compete for a preference: .VCD uses POPStarter, while Ember's own folder/image layout uses Ember automatically. External core and BIOS Ember is not embedded in Launchstation. Set an optional Ember directory under Settings → Launching → Disc & image loaders. The target game's own umbrella still needs the user's PlayStation BIOS as bios.bin (exactly 512 KB). If the target umbrella lacks ember.elf , Launchstation can copy the configured ember.elf into that umbrella once before launch. Save-safe layout The umbrella folder can be named anything and live anywhere on the device. DEVICE:/ └── MY-EMBER/ ├── ember.elf ├── bios.bin └── games/ ├── Spyro 2 (Ripto's Rage)/ │ ├── game.cue │ ├── track01.bin │ ├── MC1.vmc created/used by Ember │ └── MC2.vmc created/used by Ember └── Another Game/ └── game.bin Select a .CUE , .BIN or PS1 .EXE directly inside the game folder. Launchstation derives the bare folder name and passes that to Ember. Why loose CUE files are refused Ember can resolve looser layouts, but its memory-card path is always composed as games/<argument>/MC1.vmc and MC2.vmc . A loose games/Game.cue can boot while silently making the save path impossible. The browser therefore offers only the folder layout that can both launch and save correctly. Launch contract Ember derives its working directory from target argv[0] , so Launchstation preserves the real live path to ember.elf as target argv[0] . The bare game-folder name is the only game argument. Names containing path separators, a colon, a leading .. , or more than 180 characters are refused. USB reset and final keep-IOP handoff Ember requires a working game-device stack when control reaches it. For USB/MASS, LAUNCHSTATION first finishes background I/O and audio, prepares a clean IOP without its own PADMAN, re-discovers the USB game and ember.elf even if the drive's logical unit has changed, then executes Ember with no further IOP reset . A mismatched or ambiguous remount is refused rather than silently launching another drive. For non-USB paths the existing mounted stack is retained for handoff. On APA/PFS, the Ember partition is mounted writable with write-through for its save files. title: MMCE Backups
text: MMCE Backup History Versioned local backup protects an active MMCE card without creating an identical copy after every return. Local history The workflow exports an MMCE card image into WLE-MMCE-Backups , verifies it against the source, and publishes the completed snapshot through a same-folder rename. During export it has a .PART suffix, so interrupted writes cannot be mistaken for completed .mcd or .ps2 history or uploaded to Drive. Retention runs only after publication and never removes previous snapshots on a failed export, comparison, or rename. The retention setting can keep all history or prune older versions. Skip unchanged cards Before adding another history entry, Launchstation can compare the active card with the latest backup. If it is unchanged, the UI reports that no duplicate history was saved. Verification matters A copy is not treated as a successful backup merely because file creation returned. The backup path verifies the output before reporting success or allowing the next automatic step. Non-destructive local recovery In Settings > Storage & devices > MMCE backups , choose Recover saved card image... to browse your configured local WLE-MMCE-Backups history and select a complete .mcd or .ps2 snapshot. You can also select the snapshot in the File Browser and choose Recover as new .mcd... . To back up a specific MMCE card, highlight its .mcd under mmce0:/MemoryCards or mmce1:/MemoryCards and select Back up selected MMCE card to history... . Both routes use verified copies and leave the original emulated card untouched. From the File Browser, highlight a complete .mcd or PCSX2 .ps2 history snapshot, open the options menu and choose Recover as new .mcd... . Launchstation validates the card image first, asks you to select a USB/HDD folder, writes to a distinct .PART file, reads it back and verifies the copy, then publishes a new RECOVER-###.mcd image. Existing files and MMCE cards are not replaced or activated. Choose the separate recovery file for further inspection or manual installation after verification. To store a verified snapshot on the adapter using the unchanged sd2psXtd firmware, highlight a local USB/HDD .mcd or .ps2 file and choose Store NEW snapshot on MMCE... , then choose the adapter slot. Launchstation creates and verifies a new mmceN:/WLE-Recovered/RECOVER-###.mcd with staged .PART output. If adapter rename fails but the stage remains and the final name is free, a separate read-back-verified copy is used instead. This separate holding folder is not an active/selected card directory; the adapter does not automatically mount it. Direct replacement or activation of an emulated card remains disabled. No firmware fork, update or custom protocol is required for the new-file storage workflow. To create a new selectable card rather than a holding-area snapshot, select the completed local .mcd / .ps2 or a WLE-Recovered image in File Browser and choose Install as NEW selectable MMCE card... . Launchstation selects an entirely unused MemoryCards/PS2/CardN directory, verifies its new CardN-1.mcd image, and leaves adapter card selection unchanged. It never replaces an existing numbered, BootCard or GameID image. If rename is unsupported, the verified-copy fallback still cannot guarantee atomic power-loss publication; never select a failed/interrupted installation until that new directory has been inspected. IGR integration When Automatic IGR backup is enabled, an OPL return through WLE-IGR can capture a changed card before continuing. This keeps the safety-critical local copy independent of network/cloud availability. Browse and recover remote backup history In Tools > Google Drive backups > Browse cloud history... , explore the app-created WLE-MMCE-Backups folder on Google Drive. The paged browser lists folders and available .mcd / .ps2 snapshots. Selecting one with an uploaded SHA-256 allows verified download to a NEW RECOVER-CLOUD-###.mcd on USB/HDD. Launchstation checks the complete downloaded SHA-256, validates the card image, converts PCSX2 snapshots where needed and publishes only a verified staged recovery. Google Drive history and emulated MMCE cards are never modified; direct replacement of an MMCE card remains disabled. Cloud is additive Optional Google Drive synchronization is performed after the verified local backup. A cloud failure does not erase or invalidate the local history entry. See Native Google Drive Cloud Backup . Sync all cards Sync all cards scans both MMCE units, creates history only for changed cards, and summarizes new/unchanged/failed cards. If Google Drive is linked, pending local history is uploaded afterward. Automatic sync modes The single Automatic sync control replaces two separate toggles with three clear modes: Off , Local backup , and Local + Google Drive . Cloud mode requires a linked account. IGR helper control The MMCE backup page now exposes the existing verified WLE-IGR installer/update/remove flow directly, alongside the after-IGR destination. Recovery safety summary Action Allowed now Effect on active MMCE card Browse local history Yes Read-only Browse Drive history Yes, linked account Read-only Recover complete local snapshot to new USB/HDD .mcd Yes Unchanged Recover Drive snapshot with verified stored SHA-256 to new USB/HDD .mcd Yes Unchanged Overwrite/activate current MMCE card directly No Intentionally disabled Remote entries without the expected saved digest may be inspected but are not eligible for the verified download workflow. Incomplete .PART files never count as completed backups. For step-by-step recovery, see the wiki index and recovery guide .

title: Google Drive Cloud
text: Native Google Drive Cloud Backup Optional PS2-native OAuth 2.0 + HTTPS upload for MMCE backup history. What it does The feature links a Google account using device authorization, stores a refresh token and uploads missing backup versions from WLE-MMCE-Backups . It requests the restricted drive.file scope rather than broad access to the user's Drive. Linking Choose Link Google Drive , open google.com/device on a phone or computer and enter the code shown on the PS2. No Google Cloud project, setup files or payment details are needed: official builds include Launchstation's own OAuth client and the Google Trust Services root certificates. Cloud sidecars File Purpose WLE-CLOUD.TOK Stored refresh token after linking. WLE-CLOUD.TOK.NEW Crash-safe staging file used during token replacement. WLE-CLOUD.CNF Optional (Advanced setup): a custom OAuth client ID and secret that replace the built-in client as a pair. Template: res/WLE-CLOUD.CNF.example . WLE-CLOUD-CA.PEM Optional (Advanced setup): custom trust roots that replace the built-in Google roots; the native loader accepts at most 256 KiB. Crash-safe token replacement The staging token includes an explicit completion marker. An interrupted/incomplete .NEW file is ignored instead of superseding a valid primary token. Content-aware backup identity Each uploaded backup carries a private Drive appProperties value named wle_sha256 . A remote file is skipped only when filename and SHA-256 match. Same-name files with different content are preserved. The local backup is hashed and streamed from the same open file descriptor to avoid a validate-then-reopen race. TLS and entropy Certificate and hostname verification are mandatory. The Mbed TLS CTR-DRBG does not rely on PS2SDK's random path alone: Launchstation conditions that material with full cycle-counter samples, RTC/runtime state, a local counter and DNS/TCP timing through SHA-256. This is defense-in-depth, not a claim that the PS2 has a certified hardware TRNG. Failure behavior TCP connect, TLS handshake, reads and writes use bounded no-progress timeouts. DNS lookup itself is synchronous in PS2IP, so bad-DNS behavior remains a real-hardware edge case. Automatic IGR sync Google Drive after IGR is off by default. It cannot be enabled until Drive is linked, and it runs only after the local MMCE backup succeeds. Settings integration The MMCE backup & sync page exposes Google account management directly beside backup policy. The same native OAuth/TLS client is used; this is not a second cloud implementation. Backup controls In Settings > Storage & devices > MMCE backups, choose Backup folder : the parent of WLE-MMCE-Backups . Save changes before leaving Settings. Existing history stays in place; reinstall an existing IGR helper after changing the folder because it embeds its destination. In Google account, Back up cards & upload backs up changed MMCE cards before uploading history. Upload existing backups only uploads saved history and requires a linked account and a selected backup folder. It does not require installing the IGR helper. Backup folder... is also available in the Google account menu and saves the destination immediately. Changing an existing destination asks for confirmation; canceling or selecting the current folder leaves settings unchanged. The card status Locally backed up describes local history only, not Drive upload status. Update checks Check for updates compares the running commit with the repository's rolling latest release over HTTPS. It uses a dedicated WLE-UPDATE-CA.PEM trust root for GitHub and does not weaken or reuse Google-specific trust configuration. Remote history browsing and verified recovery Tools > Google Drive backups > Browse cloud history... shows metadata from the app-created history, page by page. Entries without a stored wle_sha256 can be inspected but cannot be used for verified download. Select a completed, digest-qualified snapshot and a destination on USB/HDD to create a separate RECOVER-CLOUD-###.mcd . The download is authenticated, size-limited and SHA-256-checked; any necessary PCSX2 image conversion and the local staged copy are validated before publishing. Existing Drive history and active MMCE cards are unchanged. MMCE recovery and safety matrix .

title: Settings Reference
text: Settings Reference Dashboard settings are grouped by purpose and retain explicit unsaved-state behavior. Major groups Group Examples Appearance Theme, selection style, icon backing, clock/date, screen position. Home & applications Application folders, startup section/view, Home shortcuts. Sound Dashboard audio and BGM behavior. Input Confirm/cancel mapping, USB keyboard, virtual keyboard layout. Launching Normal ELF IOP reset, ESR, OSDSYS, POPStarter, Ember/PS1 behavior, Neutrino and launch keys. Storage & devices Unavailable-device visibility, MMCE history and storage behavior. Network IP, netmask, gateway and network-oriented feature controls. System Core runtime options and maintenance actions. PS2 clock without a working CMOS battery Use Settings > System > Set PS2 clock manually... and enter YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS . Launchstation validates the date, writes the PS2 RTC and verifies the readback. With a dead clock battery, the time may need setting again after power loss. Colored Game ID launch bars Game ID color output for ELF/application launches is off by default on new configurations. It remains available in Settings > Launching > Game ID output for RetroGEM-compatible display adapters. Previously saved configurations retain their selected value until changed. Theme-matched controller button icons Settings > Appearance > Control icon backings controls whether face-button and D-pad symbols receive a theme-derived badge. When disabled, the symbols render without the backing. Button symbols are generated from the built-in vector atlas and need no external icon PNGs. Unsaved state Settings compare current serialized values with the session snapshot. Touching a control and returning it to the original value does not leave a false dirty flag. Save failures remain visible and can be retried. Path pickers Program/file settings use the native browser picker. POPStarter and Neutrino have explicit ELF path fields. Ember uses an Ember directory picker instead: the folder name/location is arbitrary, but the save-safe umbrella still contains ember.elf , bios.bin and games/<Game>/ . When a selected game's own umbrella lacks ember.elf , the configured Ember directory can supply it to that device automatically. VCD remains POPStarter; CUE/BIN/EXE remains Ember. Unavailable devices Show unavailable devices controls whether confirmed-missing devices are displayed. Hidden devices are removed from navigation as well as drawing. Unprobed devices remain actionable. Reset actions Display/theme reset actions restore known project defaults so users do not need to manually reverse each visual setting. MMCE backup & sync page The IGR helper row reports Current , Outdated , Not installed or Partial / mixed by comparing installed helper bytes with the helper this build would install for the current application and backup paths. Entering this page is treated as an explicit request for live MMCE status: if a backup destination is configured and MMCE is not already running, the MMCE stack is started on demand before the read-only status scan. A startup failure is shown instead of leaving the page silently at Not checked . This page groups the controls that previously lived across Settings and Tools: Sync all cards, Automatic sync, IGR helper, After IGR, Language, retention, backup format, Google account, Check for updates and About. Existing lower-level backup/cloud routines are reused rather than duplicated. Native update install Check for updates validates ancestry against the rolling latest release. The updater selects the standard or DS34 PSU package for the running variant, verifies its advertised SHA-256 and contents over trusted HTTPS, stages the verified ELF and then replaces the running app's ELF using a .BAK rollback file. The verified four-file PSU can restore missing updater CA and BGM sidecars, but it does not overwrite existing customized sidecars. Interrupted .UPDATE / .PACKAGE staging files are preserved for manual recovery rather than silently truncated. Restart LAUNCHSTATION to execute the new build. Older update clients may require a one-time manual package install. MMCE sync status Sync all cards reports Checking... , All synced , or the number of card images still pending. The pending check is read-only: it compares live MMCE card images with the newest local history without creating, pruning or deleting backups. PCSX2-format history is compared in memory rather than by creating a temporary conversion. Opening this Settings page starts MMCE on demand when live card status is needed, even when MMCE auto-start is disabled. The page shows Starting MMCE... during initialization and reports a startup failure explicitly rather than leaving the status indefinitely at Not checked . The Google account row similarly reports whether the native Drive account is linked. Current Home, Apps and Files placement Home includes the Applications library and Last folder shortcut. Files runs the native File Browser directly; separate Apps and Devices labels are retained only where the old internal section identifiers require compatibility. Tools is where classic MISC commands live. MMCE and Drive recovery The MMCE backups Settings page can select a local snapshot for non-destructive recovery. The Google account/Tools cloud menu can browse remote history and recover a SHA-256-qualified snapshot into a new image on USB/HDD. Neither flow automatically replaces a live MMCE card. Recovery details .

title: Display, Themes & BGM
text: Display, Themes & BGM The dashboard is PS2-inspired but deliberately configurable rather than forcing one presentation. Selection presentation Selection style can be changed instead of forcing a single hue/glow. Selected and unselected device cards use the same geometry; focus adds emphasis without resizing/reflowing the card. Icon backing Control/menu icon backing can be enabled or disabled explicitly. This option came from tester feedback rather than being baked into a single theme. Clock and date The dashboard clock can follow system 12/24-hour behavior or theme overrides, optionally show seconds and use configured date order/placement. File metadata retains seconds independently of the clock setting. Motion Top tabs, selection movement, OSD orbs and marquee effects use bounded smooth animation. The former fast sinusoidal header overshoot was removed because it could appear as top-of-dashboard video flicker on interlaced displays. Custom wallpaper: 4:3 aspect ratio Make your wallpaper on a 4:3 canvas . Use 640 × 480 PNG to preserve detail, or 320 × 240 for a smaller, lower-memory image like the starter example. Launchstation preserves aspect ratio, center-crops wider or taller inputs, and fills the screen. The decoder keeps wallpapers inside a 640 × 512 box, so a 4:3 source can retain 640 × 480 pixels. Smaller sources are not enlarged during decoding. A 640 × 480 texture uses about 1.17 MiB of decoded memory, four times the 320 × 240 option. This improves image detail at the existing output modes; it does not itself change the video output resolution. The 640 × 448 logical UI coordinate system is not the required artwork ratio. Example PNG: 320 × 240, exactly 4:3, with illustrative guides. You can use it as a test wallpaper or replace the drawing with your own artwork. Download example background.png · Matching theme.cfg · Complete example folder Format and composition tips Format: PNG, maximum file size 1.5 MB and source dimensions 2048 × 2048. A non-interlaced RGB or indexed 320 × 240 PNG is an easy choice. Safe area: keep important subject matter away from the extreme edges. CRT overscan and screen centering vary, and dashboard panels or hints may cover parts of the image. Contrast: use a dark or subdued background behind text and adjust theme brightness, panel opacity and text colours if needed. Other ratios: 320 × 256 is 5:4, and 320 × 224 is 10:7; both are supported inputs but are not the ideal 4:3 canvas. 16:9 sources are cropped horizontally. How to enable one For a single image, open Settings > Appearance > Customize theme > Background > Wallpaper image... , then choose a PNG and save your Settings changes. To load the example theme, place theme.cfg and background.png together inside a folder under THEMES/ next to the Launchstation ELF (or in the dashboard configuration folder). Choose Settings > Appearance > Theme files & resets > Load theme from folder... , select that folder and save. For a theme.cfg file, background = image and image = background.png select the static wallpaper. The separate wallpaper = focused option uses the artwork of the selected application and is not needed for a custom static image. Missing or invalid wallpaper files fall back to the theme gradient. Background music BGM.ADP ships in the current rolling ZIP/PSU packages but remains optional for standalone ELF installs. Put it next to the executable when installed manually. A missing music file does not prevent the dashboard from booting. Website cursor orbs The GitHub Pages site has a separate top-header cursor-orb toggle. Orbs are on by default on desktop and off by default on mobile/coarse-pointer devices. Your choice is saved locally, and switching off stops the animation loop. This does not change the PS2 dashboard theme. Reset display/theme The reset action restores video mode/centering and project theme defaults, useful when experimentation makes text, selection or offsets difficult to recover manually.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting Identify the failing layer first: hardware/device, filesystem, Launchstation launch preparation, external core, or the target application/game. Device says Not checked Open it. Not checked is intentionally actionable: the lazy driver has not yet established presence. A confirmed Not connected result is different. USB path/unit changed Do not assume mass0: . Multiple drives, MX4SIO and attach order can affect unit numbering. Start from the dashboard's USB / MASS device and let the root discovery logic identify what is available. PS2 ISO will not start Browse/read the ISO from the same source device. Confirm it is an ISO9660 image. Set a Neutrino path explicitly to remove search-order ambiguity. Confirm Neutrino has modern config/system.toml or legacy adjacent system.toml . Try a known-good ISO on the same backend. PS1 VCD will not start Confirm the VCD is in a supported POPStarter layout, then set POPStarter explicitly. HDD POPS layouts have special argument construction; a raw browser path is not necessarily a valid POPStarter command line. Google Drive link/upload fails Confirm network/IP first, then PS2 clock/time, then any custom OAuth client or CA bundle under Advanced setup. Certificate validation can fail when the RTC is materially wrong. DNS remains synchronous in PS2IP and can behave differently from the later socket timeout path. Colored bars before opening ELFs Launchstation can intentionally draw a short Game ID identification signal for compatible video adapters. To disable the colored bars, open Settings > Launching > Game ID output and turn off the application Game ID launch signal. Normal start-up boot-check text is hidden in production builds. Top-of-dashboard flicker The known fast selector oscillation has been removed. If flicker persists, report video mode, display/cable, interlace/progressive mode, theme, and whether the symptom occurs in the classic UI too. Good bug report Exact commit/build and package or packed ELF SHA-256. Console model and video mode. Source device/backend and filesystem. Minimal reproduction steps. Whether classic browser and dashboard differ. For Neutrino/POPStarter, external-core version and resolved path.

title: Privacy Policy
text: Privacy Policy Launchstation is free, open-source PlayStation 2 homebrew. It has no accounts, no analytics and no servers of its own. This page explains the little data it handles and where it goes. Summary Launchstation does not collect, sell or share personal data. There is no telemetry, advertising or tracking. Everything Launchstation stores stays on your own PS2 storage (memory card, USB, HDD and similar). Network features run only when you use them, and talk directly to the services listed below. Google Drive backup (optional) If you choose Link Google Drive , you authorize Launchstation on a phone or computer with a short code from Google. Launchstation requests only the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file scope, which lets it see and manage only the files it creates (your memory-card backups in the WLE-MMCE-Backups folder). It cannot read the rest of your Google Drive. Google returns an authorization (refresh) token, which Launchstation saves in WLE-CLOUD.TOK beside its settings on your own device. The token is sent only to Google, over verified HTTPS, to upload, list or download your backups. Launchstation's developers never receive your token, your backups or your Google account details. Uploaded files carry a private checksum ( wle_sha256 ) so unchanged backups are not uploaded twice. To stop access, choose Disconnect Google Drive in Launchstation, which deletes the local token, and/or remove Launchstation at Google Account > Third-party access . Files already uploaded stay in your Drive until you delete them. Launchstation's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy , including the Limited Use requirements. Other network features Check for updates contacts the GitHub API and downloads release files from GitHub when you ask it to. GitHub's own privacy statement applies to those requests. Clock synchronization , when used, asks public time servers (such as time.google.com , time.cloudflare.com or pool.ntp.org ) for the current time. No personal data is sent. Network file sharing (host/UDPFS and similar) connects only to computers you configure on your own network. Like any internet request, these services can see your IP address. Launchstation adds no identifiers of its own. Children Launchstation does not knowingly collect data from anyone, including children. Changes and contact Changes to this policy are published on this page and in the project's GitHub repository . Questions can be raised as a GitHub issue or sent to the support email shown on the Google consent screen. Last updated: 12 October 2026.
